author: implementation-agent

findings.summary: Search-mode options are implemented as span elements with button roles instead of native buttons.
findings.consequence: The component has to recreate native keyboard and activation behavior manually, and future changes can easily miss browser-provided button semantics such as disabled state, form ownership, and consistent assistive-technology handling.
findings.evidence: The mode selector renders `<span role="button" tabindex="0">` for each interactive search mode, with custom click, Enter, and Space handlers, inside the search form.
findings.recommendation: Use a native `<button type="button">` for each search-mode control, keep the existing `aria-pressed` state, and preserve the current visual classes/styles on the button.
verification: Checked the associated setSearchMode and selectedMode handlers in app/pages/sök.vue lines 963-1033.

findings.summary: The gender Listbox button is named only by its current value, not by the filter purpose.
findings.consequence: A screen-reader user encountering the collapsed control hears a selected value such as `Alla författare` without an explicit indication that this is the author-gender filter, unlike the adjacent multiselect controls whose placeholders identify their purpose.
findings.evidence: The gender filter renders `<ListboxButton class="select2-selection select2-selection--single">` with only the rendered `genderLabel` inside and no aria-label, aria-labelledby, or visible label tied to the control.
findings.recommendation: Give the ListboxButton a purpose-bearing accessible name, for example `:aria-label="`Författarkön: ${genderLabel}`"`, while keeping the visible selected label unchanged.
